subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript model of a flamingo using realistic proportions, roughly 1.3-1.4 meters tall, standing in shallow water with feet at ground level, and sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting with the hip root position.

For the legs, I'm working out the joint chain -- hip, knee-like bend near the body, tarsus, and ankle down to the webbed foot -- trying to match proportions so the limb lengths sum close to the actual vertical distance from hip to floor.

I'll bend the knee backward with a hock-like joint, matching the flamingo's characteristic backward-pointing tibiotarsal joint. For the leg chain, I'll use three named points—hip, knee, ankle—so the chain produces span joints plus a tip joint at the ankle, which becomes the foot attachment point for the webbed toes.

Now I'm working out the toe placement: forward-extending toes from the ankle with a membrane between them for the webbed effect, but I'm running into coordinate issues since the ankle's local frame is aimed downward along the limb's end tangent. I'm simplifying by just setting absolute foot/toe heights near ground level (~0.012) with a small ankle offset above that, rather than fighting with local relative coordinates.

Settling on simplifying the toe webbing into a rigid slab across tips and ankle, acknowledging the rig is getting complex but moving on to the remaining body parts—wings, neck, head, beak, eyes, tail. I'm sketching the spine as a chain of joints from hips through chest, using a catmull curve for the path, then planning to sweep a surface over that spine chain with a radius function to form the body.

I'm shaping the body's radius profile so it's thin at the tail, thickest mid-body, and tapers again toward the chest, tilting the spine curve forward and up to approximate a flamingo's horizontal-leaning posture with the tail rear-low. I'm now consolidating this into one bodyPath curve and defining the spine chain off the hips joint, naming the segments for the sweep to follow.

Setting up spine chain joints...

Now for the neck, I need an S-curve shape flowing from chest up and forward, then curling back before the head leans forward again. I'll use five points along this path so the chain produces four named neck segments plus a head tip joint oriented along the final tangent direction.

For the actual sweep, I'm giving it a thick base radius around 0.055 that tapers down toward the head, matching a flamingo's proportions. Then for the head itself, I'll just use a small stretched sphere as an ellipsoid shape attached to the head joint, scaled slightly longer along one axis to suggest a beak-ward profile.

Eyes go symmetric on both sides using a mirrored position offset from the head center, small pale yellow spheres placed just above and forward. For the beak, I'm planning a bent sweep curve attached at the front of the head, pale pink at the base and darkening toward a black tip, bowing downward to capture that characteristic flamingo hook.

Now I'm sketching the folded wing structure: shoulder joints on either side of the body near the back, tapering down to wing tips tucked along the flank, built as a swept shape mirroring left and right.

Working out the wing outline coordinates and confirming the thickness axis runs along X so the wing sits flat in the side plane, tapering from shoulder to tip. I'm positioning each wing mirrored at x=±0.13 near the back joint, planning to rigidly bind it to the spine rather than a separate chain.

Now I'm layering a black flight-feather slab over the wingtip with its own outline, nudging it slightly outward in X to avoid z-fighting with the base coral gradient wing, and double-checking how the local u/v coordinates map given the extrude direction.

For the tail, I'm deciding it can be minimal—maybe a small pale slab at the tip or just a joint—since flamingo tails are short and mostly hidden by folded wings.

Now I'm setting up the leg rig: a rose-colored hip-knee-ankle chain parented to the hips, built from a limb call between hip and foot points with a bend direction for the knee joint.

Checking the leg geometry, I realize the hip-to-foot vertical distance exceeds the combined segment lengths, so I need to adjust either the hip height or segment lengths to keep the leg within reach.

I'm revising to make the knee higher up, matching the real flamingo anatomy where the thigh is hidden under feathers near the belly and only the lower leg is the visible pink segment, so I'll color the thigh portion to match the body rather than the leg.

For the chain sweep itself, I'm setting up a color band that switches from body color to leg color partway along the leg, roughly where the knee joint sits, and adding a small sphere at that knee joint for the knobbly-knee detail.

Now I'm thinking through leg taper radius (thicker thigh, thinner ankle), skipping tail plume details for time, and working out webbed feet by placing toe tips as small offsets from the ankle joint, fumbling a bit with how to type the ankle/tip joint reference in TypeScript.

Building toe capsule rods and web polygon...

I'm checking the foot placement so the toes rest just above ground level, then considering whether to add a thin shallow-water disc beneath the feet to represent standing in water, making sure it stays below the model's lowest points.

I'll add a subtle ring ripple in the water, keeping it modest. For colors, I'm picking a candy pink body with coral gradient wings, dark near-black accents, pale pink beak, and pale yellow eyes with black pupils, staying well under the color limit. Then I'm working out the body sweep radii along the spine chain, using a piecewise profile that's thin at the tail, thickest through the midsection, and tapering toward the neck and head.

Now I'm defining the neck chain's path points and parenting it to the chest joint of the spine, making sure the sweep covers all the way to the head tip. I'm positioning the head sphere at the end of the neck, then building a curved beak that bends downward with a thinner, darker tip, and placing the eyes laterally on the head with small dark pupils slightly protruding from the eye surface.

For the wings, I'm sketching an outline in local coordinates running from the shoulder back toward the tail, adding a separate darker wingtip shape layered on top, and extruding both with a gradient from pink to coral, parented to the back joint of the spine. I'm also adding a small coral tail fan extruded horizontally near the tail joint, and placing a couple of light-colored ripple rings plus a shallow water cylinder beneath the model.

Finally, I'm setting up the leg chains from hip to foot using three-point limb paths, naming the joints for hip, knee, and ankle, and sweeping each leg with a tapering radius and a color band that shifts from a feathered thigh tone near the body to the leg's main color below the knee.

Still building the body parts — eyes, beak, wings, tail plume, legs with knobbly knees, webbed toes, and the water pool with ripple rings. I'm working through placement math for each part relative to their parent bones, making sure proportions and colors (pink, coral, rose, black, yellow) stay consistent, then assembling everything into the final exported model and returning the root.
